# Privacy Policy

_Effective October 9, 2026_

Longstead is published by Core Hermit and is part of a family of private, on-device apps. It is built to work without collecting your data. This policy explains what happens to information when you use Longstead on iPhone and Mac.

## The short version
- We do **not** collect, store, sell, or share your personal data. We have no servers that receive it.
- There are **no accounts, no ads, no analytics, and no tracking**.
- Your profile, accounts, balances, plans, and conversations are stored **on your device** and stay there unless you choose to export or share them.
- All calculations run **on your device**, and by default so do the AI features. The app does not use Apple's Private Cloud Compute and contains no cloud AI service of its own. If you choose to connect your own model server (for example Ollama or LM Studio), your questions go to that server instead (see AI processing).

## Information stored on your device
Longstead stores the following only in its own storage on your device:
- your profile: name, age, planned retirement age, life expectancy, filing status, state, spending, Social Security estimates, and risk tolerance;
- the accounts you enter: names, types, institutions, balances, contributions, and expected returns;
- plans (projects) you create and any files you export;
- your conversations with the in-app advisors and the analyses they produce, kept per plan (the app does not index or search them to build later answers);
- your settings, a list of your downloaded AI models, the AI model files themselves, and a log of the network requests the app makes. If you connect a model server that needs an API key, the key is kept in your device's Keychain, not in your settings or exports.

We cannot access any of it. The app asks the system to leave this storage out of iCloud and device backups, so it is not copied to iCloud by the app. That also means it is **not recoverable from a backup**: export plans you care about (Profile > Plan management > Export plan) and keep the file somewhere you control.

## AI processing
Advisor answers are generated **on your device**, using Apple's on-device Foundation Models (Apple Intelligence) and, if you choose to download them, open-source models that run locally using Apple's MLX framework. Tax, withdrawal, and simulation figures are calculated by the app's own code, not estimated by an AI model. By default your questions and plan data are not sent to any server for AI processing.

If you choose to connect your own model server (Ollama, LM Studio, or any server that speaks the OpenAI-compatible chat API), an advisor set to use it sends what the model sees (your question and, depending on the advisor, plan details) to that server, and the server's operator handles it under their own terms. The app treats an address on your own computer or network (localhost, 127.x, *.local, 10.x, 172.16 to 172.31.x, 192.168.x) as yours; for any other address it shows a warning that your questions and plan details would be sent to that server. These requests appear in Settings > Network audit log. You can disconnect the server at any time.

## Network connections
Longstead has no server of ours that your data is sent to. By default the only network request the app makes to a third party is a model download that you start (the app also checks your own computer for Ollama at localhost, which does not leave your computer). It makes only these connections. None of them include your profile, balances, or conversations, except a model server you connect yourself:

| Connection | When | What is sent |
|---|---|---|
| **huggingface.co** (and the content-delivery hosts it redirects to) | Only when you tap Download on an AI model | A request for that model's files. Hugging Face sees your IP address, standard request details, and the model you asked for. |
| **A tax-data feed address you enter yourself** (optional) | Only if you type a feed address in Settings > Tax data. The app then checks it in the foreground about every 30 days while "Allow yearly tax-data updates" is on. By default no address is set and nothing is requested. | A request for tax-table files. The host you entered sees your IP address and standard request details. |
| **A model server you connect yourself** (optional), such as Ollama or LM Studio | Only if you connect one in Settings > Your own model server, or Ollama is found on your computer at localhost. | Your questions to the advisors and the details the model needs, and requests for the server's model list. On iPhone and iPad, iOS asks for Local Network permission when a server on your network is used. |
| **Links you tap**, such as this policy | When you tap them | Opens in your browser. |

Some buttons open a page in your web browser, for example **Install Ollama** (ollama.com) and the link to your Social Security account (www.ssa.gov). The app itself sends nothing to those sites; your browser visits them under their own privacy policies.

The requests the app makes are recorded in Settings > Network audit log on your device, so you can see them. Apart from these, the app works offline. These services handle requests under their own privacy policies, and we do not receive any information from them about you.

## Mac download
The Mac version is available through the Mac App Store and TestFlight, and as a signed, notarized download from our website and GitHub Releases. It behaves the same way as the iPhone version: no account, no analytics, no tracking, and the same optional connections above. It does not include an automatic update service, so it does not contact us to check for new versions. Your data is stored in your user Library folder (`~/Library/Application Support/RetirementPlanner`). Downloading the app from our website or GitHub is subject to the privacy practices of the host (for example, a web server or GitHub may log your IP address and the file requested).

## TestFlight, Apple, Hugging Face, and downloads
- **TestFlight and the App Store.** If you install through TestFlight or the App Store, Apple handles your Apple Account, purchases and downloads, crash reports, and any feedback you choose to send, under Apple's privacy policy. TestFlight feedback and crash reports you submit are delivered to us through Apple and may include your email address, device model, and what you write or attach. We use them only to fix problems and reply to you.
- **Apple Intelligence.** On-device Apple Intelligence processing is governed by Apple's terms. We do not receive it.
- **Hugging Face** (and any tax-data host or model server you enter) receive the requests described above and keep their own server logs under their own policies. If you download the Mac app from GitHub Releases, GitHub handles that download under its own policy.

## Data retention and deletion
We hold no personal data about you. On your device, the data stays until you delete it. You can delete individual accounts, plans, and conversations inside the app. **Settings > Your data > Erase all data** deletes all plans, accounts, conversations, settings, the network log, and the models stored inside the app, and returns the app to first-launch setup. Deleting the app on iPhone also removes its data. On Mac, after deleting the app you can remove the folder `~/Library/Application Support/RetirementPlanner`. On Mac, downloaded model files may be kept in the Hugging Face cache that is shared with other tools; Erase all data does not touch that cache, so delete it yourself if you want those files gone. Files you exported or shared are copies you control; delete them yourself.

## Security
Your data is kept in the app's storage on your device and is protected by your device's own protections (for example, the passcode and data protection on iPhone, and FileVault and your user account on Mac). We do not transmit it, so there is no server copy to be breached; the exception is a model server you connect yourself, which receives what you ask it and is outside our control. Network requests use HTTPS, except that your own model server may use a plain local address such as http://localhost:11434. Anyone who can unlock your device or sign in to your Mac account may be able to see your data, so use a passcode and keep your operating system up to date. No method of storage is perfectly secure.

## Sharing and exports
The app only shares something when you ask it to, for example when you export or share a plan or a conversation. You choose where it goes (such as Messages, Mail, or Files), and that destination's own privacy terms apply. Plan files you export (.retplan) are unencrypted JSON that contain your plan data. The app saves them wherever you choose, and they leave the app's protection once saved, so store and share them carefully (for example in an encrypted folder). Anyone with the file can read it.

## International users and legal bases
The app works on your device and we do not receive your personal data, so we do not transfer it across borders. The only data flows are the requests you trigger to Hugging Face (and to a tax-data host or a model server if you enter one), which operate globally and may process your IP address outside your country) and to Apple. If data protection law such as the EU or UK GDPR applies, then to the extent any processing is ours, it is limited to the on-device processing needed to provide the features you ask for (performance of the service you requested) and the optional tax-data check you can turn on by entering a feed address. Where a request is made only because you tapped Download, it is made at your request.

## Your rights
Because we don't collect personal data, we hold no personal data about you to access, correct, port, or delete, and you control all of it on your device.
- **California (CCPA/CPRA).** We do not sell or share personal information (as those terms are defined in California law), we do not use it for targeted advertising, and we do not collect sensitive personal information. You may ask what we hold; the answer is that we hold none from the app. We will not discriminate against you for asking.
- **EU, UK, and similar laws (GDPR).** You may have rights to access, rectify, erase, restrict, object to, or port personal data, and to complain to your data protection authority. We hold no personal data collected through the app, so there is nothing for us to provide, but if you contact us (for example for support) we will answer your request about the emails we hold.
Email wavypix@gmail.com to exercise a right or ask a question.

## Children
Longstead is a retirement-planning tool and is not directed to children under 13 (or under 16 where that is the age of digital consent). We do not knowingly collect information from children, and the app collects no information from anyone.

## Changes
If this policy changes, we'll update the effective date and publish the new version in the app and at https://corehermit.github.io/longstead/privacy/. If a change is material we will say so in the app or in the release notes.
